Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

pipeflow 0.5.0.9012

Breaking changes

  • as.function() lost the argument bind. Bind the inputs of the function with params of pip_add() instead, as for any other step function, e.g. pip_add(outer, "step", f, params = list(input_df = ~split)).
  • The argument cache of as.function() is now TRUE (the default) or FALSE instead of the number of inner pipelines to keep.

New features

  • out of as.function() can be a function. It is called with a light copy of the run inner pipeline, and its result is the result of the function, e.g. out = \(p) pip_collect(p, by = "tags").
  • New pip_inner(x, step) returns the inner pipelines that the function of a step, made by as.function(), has kept: one per partition key for a mapped step. Use it e.g. to debug an inner run.

Changes

  • A function made by as.function() keeps one inner pipeline per outer step and partition key, so a later call only reruns the inner steps whose params or inputs changed, for any number of partitions. This also works for inputs bound via params of pip_add().

Documentation

  • The “Nested pipelines” vignette shows a function as out and pip_inner(), and its “Full control” example forwards the step’s params with pip_set_params(p, list(...)).

pipeflow 0.5.0.9011

Documentation

  • The cheat sheet shows “Ways to connect steps” again on page 2.

pipeflow 0.5.0.9010

Breaking changes

  • pip_set_params() binds a param to a step if its value is a one-sided formula, e.g. pip_set_params(p, list(model = ~fit)), as a formula does in the defaults of a step function and in params of pip_add(). Before, the formula was set as value. To set a formula as value, give it as a string and turn it into a formula in the step, e.g. with as.formula(). Because of this, as.function() no longer turns such a value into a reference to a step of the outer pipeline.

New features

  • pip_set_params() can bind params to steps. The param is bound in all selected, unlocked steps that have it unbound, which must come after the step it is bound to; a view selects the steps to bind. A bound param is no longer unbound, and setting the same binding again does nothing.

Changes

  • The warning of pip_set_params() about unknown params no longer shows the call.

pipeflow 0.5.0.9009

Breaking changes

  • params of pip_add() and pip_replace() now override the defaults of fun, as they did before 0.4.0. Before, the defaults of fun won and pip_add() warned that the values in params were dropped. A formula in params makes the parameter a reference to another step, also if its default is a value.

New features

  • params can give a value to parameters of fun that have no default, so that existing functions can be steps without a wrapper, e.g. pip_add(p, "avg", mean, params = list(x = ~data, na.rm = TRUE)).

Changes

  • params of pip_add() and pip_replace() must be a list with unique names.
  • The params of a step list the arguments of fun first, in their order, followed by the other params (before: the given params came first).
  • pip_add() and pip_replace() point to as.function() if fun is a pipeline.
  • Replacing a step with one that references a step which comes after it now reports “cannot reference steps that come after the replaced step”, matching pip_add(), instead of “cannot reference unknown steps”.

Bug fixes

  • Copying steps between pipelines with p[i] <- q[j] dropped the params that were given via params (e.g. extra params passed via ...), and took references from the defaults of the function, ignoring a renamed upstream step.
  • Copying steps with p[i] <- q[j], also onto themselves, resolved relative references such as ~-1 again, so that after inserting or removing a step, the copied step depended on another step or failed. A copied step now depends on the same steps as the source step, by name.
  • rbind() dropped the arguments with a NULL value from the step functions of the second pipeline, so that these steps failed with “unused argument”.

pipeflow 0.5.0.9008

New features

  • rbind() of pipelines gained the argument bind, a named list of one-sided formulas as in as.function(), e.g. rbind(a, b, bind = list(data = ~prep)). It binds unbound params of the second pipeline to steps of the first one, so that the pipelines are connected without editing the second one first.

Bug fixes

  • Steps with non-syntactic names, e.g. "source data", can be referenced with backticks, x = ~`source data`. Before, pip_add() reported them as unknown steps.
  • rbind() no longer fails if the second pipeline references a step with a non-syntactic name, e.g. after pip_rename().

pipeflow 0.5.0.9007

New features

  • as.function() gained the argument on_error. Set to "continue", the inner pipeline is run as pip_run(on_error = "continue") runs it: inner steps that do not depend on a failed step still run, and a ~try(step) reference inside the inner pipeline receives the failure. The function still fails if one of the steps named in out failed or was not run because an input failed.
  • as.function() gained the argument lgr, the logger of the inner run. The inner pipeline is still run silently by default (lgr = NULL), but its steps can now be logged, e.g. as.function(x, lgr = pipeflow_lgr).

pipeflow 0.5.0.9006

New features

  • as.function() turns a pipeline into a function whose arguments are the unbound params of the pipeline, so that a pipeline can be a step of another pipeline, e.g. pip_add(outer, "step", as.function(inner), params = list(df = ~split)). The params of the inner pipeline become params of the outer step, the exec modes map it over partitions, and the function keeps the inner pipelines it has run, so that a changed param only reruns the affected inner steps. See ?as.function.pipeflow and the “Nested pipelines” vignette.

pipeflow 0.5.0.9005

Changes

  • Adding a step that references a step which exists but comes after the insertion point now reports “cannot reference steps that come after the insertion point” instead of “cannot reference unknown steps”.
  • The error raised when pip_add(), pip_clone() or rbind() is given a view now points at x[, view = FALSE].

Bug fixes

  • v[, view = FALSE] returned the view instead of a standalone pipeline of the covered steps, silently ignoring view = FALSE.

pipeflow 0.5.0.9004

New features

  • `pip_param_value<-`() is the write side of pip_param_value(): a generic that turns a plain value into the value stored in a step, so that pip_set_params() keeps the annotations of a stored object when it is given a plain value.
  • pip_set_params() gained ..., which is passed on to the methods of `pip_param_value<-`(). It now determines the value to store for every affected step before it changes anything: if a method fails, nothing is set and an error of class pipeflow_set_params_error reports all failures at once.

Documentation

  • pip_get_params() notes that a view excludes locked steps, pip_get_params(p[!locked]).

pipeflow 0.5.0.9003

New features

  • pip_output_value() is a generic for annotating the output of a step when the step returns, for example to stamp a result with the step it came from and the time of the run. It is applied once to the output, and once per partition for a partitioned output, which gets its key in ctx$key. See the new vignette “Annotated step outputs”.

pipeflow 0.5.0.9002

Breaking changes

  • .self is released when a step returns, so that step outputs no longer keep the pipeline alive. A step that returns a function which refers to .self now fails with object '.self' not found when that function is called after the run.

pipeflow 0.5.0.9001

Documentation

  • New hexagon logo with the package name, used in the README and as pkgdown logo and favicons. The source is logo/logo.svg.
  • New two-page cheat sheet (cheatsheet/pipeflow-cheatsheet.pdf), shown in the README between “Installation” and “Usage”.
  • Shorter README introduction and “Why pipeflow?” list.
  • The pkgdown site is centered again, and its home page shows the logo left of the package name.

pipeflow 0.5.0

CRAN release: 2026-10-13

Breaking changes

  • v[["view"]] returns the names of the covered steps instead of row indices.
  • .self is only made available in step functions that refer to it, i.e. if the name .self appears in the function body.
  • pip_replace() by default now keeps the tags and the execution mode of the replaced step.

New features

  • pip_run(on_error = "continue") continues the run of unaffected steps after a step fails with an error.
  • allow mitigation of inputs from failed steps via ~try() references (x = ~try(step)), e.g. by creating fallback results for failed steps.
  • pip_param_value() is a generic for unwrapping parameter values, enabling users to set pipeline parameters that consist of non-trivial types or classes.
  • pip_set_params() gains unknown = c("warn", "ignore", "error") for parameters that no step defines, and force = TRUE to outdate steps even if the values are identical.
  • pip_run_state() returns the run state of a pipeline or view.
  • The default logger pipeflow_lgr() is exported, so custom loggers can build on it.
  • Pipelines survive saveRDS() and readRDS(), and can be sent to other R processes (see ?pip_new).

Changes

  • pip_set_params() no longer outdates steps if the values are identical to the stored ones.
  • Errors from pip_run() name the step (step 'fit': ...) and have class pipeflow_step_error with the fields step and parent. A failing partition key gives a pipeflow_key_error with key and parent.
  • Views keep the name of their pipeline (before: "<name> view").
  • Views keep track of their steps instead of row numbers, so they stay valid when steps are added, removed, renamed or replaced.
  • pip_run() also re-runs a "done" step if one of its inputs was executed in the same run.
  • A run stopped by halt() ends in run state "halted" (before: "ready").
  • pip_add() and pip_replace() warn if params contain names that are also arguments of fun.
  • print() now shows conditions, matrices, arrays, tables, functions and environments in the out column in short form, e.g. <error/simpleError>.

Bug fixes

  • Steps that never ran stay "new", and a run only outdates the steps downstream of steps it executed.
  • x[[step, j]] on a view read the wrong row.
  • Copies made by pip_clone(), p[] or p[i, view = FALSE] shared .self with the original.
  • pip_set_params() no longer warns about parameters defined only in locked steps.
  • pip_add() and pip_replace() reject primitive functions such as sum with a clear error, and pip_add() calls .self a reserved parameter name.
  • A step that references the same step more than once no longer warns about an existing edge.

Documentation

  • New vignettes “Handling failures” and “Annotated parameter values”.
  • “Get started”, “Nested pipelines”, “Self-modifying pipelines” and “Combine pipelines” cover identical values, unknown = "ignore", when .self is available, and saving pipelines.
  • The benchmark vignette was revised.
  • The package website is built by a GitHub Actions workflow on release tags.

pipeflow 0.4.0

CRAN release: 2026-09-27

New features

  • Pipeline functions can be called as methods on the pipeline object, e.g. p$add(...), p$run(...), p$set_params(...), …
  • The extract and replace operators gained new capabilities:
    • two-index extraction (p[[step, "out"]]),
    • negative row indices in p[...] and p[i, j] <- value,
    • boolean filters in p[...] (data.table-style expressions),
    • cross-pipeline assignment to copy steps between pipelines,
    • step removal via p[[step, "step"]] <- NULL,
    • time stamps via p[[step, "time"]] <- value,
    • setting or replacing views via p[["view"]] <- ....
  • pip_collect() (formerly pip_collect_out()) supports grouping via a by argument, as.table = TRUE to return a compact table, and a simplify argument to control flattening of single-step groups.
  • pip_data() provides direct access to the underlying step table.
  • pip_graph() (formerly pip_get_graph()) returns visNetwork-compatible graph data. The old function names remain available as deprecated aliases.
  • The derived columns depends, unbound and nodeId are read-only and can’t be assigned directly.
  • pip_view() gains a join = "union" argument to combine filters as a logical OR.
  • .self is now automatically available inside every step function (and is a protected parameter name), enabling pipelines to modify themselves at runtime, including .self$restart() and .self$halt().

Changes

  • The columns of the internal step table were reordered and nodeId is now shown in the full print view (cols = "all").
  • The dependencies on lgr and jsonlite were removed.

Bug fixes

  • pip_rename() no longer corrupts the parameters of single-step pipelines.
  • Running a view now resolves upstream dependencies correctly.

Documentation

  • New vignettes: “Working with pipeline views” and “Nested pipelines”.
  • Help pages of related functions were consolidated (extract/replace operators, dim/length, lock/unlock, tag/untag, set_params/get_params).
  • pip_run() documents the runtime control flow (restart(), halt()), and pip_add() gained an example for the after argument.

pipeflow 0.3.0

CRAN release: 2026-06-15

New features

  • C++ DAG engine (src/dag.cpp): All graph operations (node/edge add/remove, topological ordering, reachability queries) run at C++ speed via Rcpp, eliminating R object overhead for dependency resolution.
  • New pip_* API: Functional API replacing the R6 Pipeline class — pip_new(), pip_add(), pip_run(), pip_replace(), pip_clone(), pip_bind(), pip_view(), pip_tag()/pip_untag(), etc.
  • Execution modes (auto/split/reduce/plain): Native support for map-reduce style workflows where steps split output into named partitions and downstream steps auto-map over them.
  • Dependency validation at definition time: pip_add(), pip_replace(), and pip_remove() fail fast on broken references.
  • New pkgdown-only article pipeflow vs targets (vignettes/articles/v07-vs-targets.Rmd) with an 18-row feature comparison table and benchmarks.

Breaking changes

  • Legacy pipe_* functions and Pipeline R6 class are deprecated (preserved as aliases in R/aliases.R, R/pipelineR6.R).
  • pip_collect_out() no longer accepts grouped or by parameters. It returns a flat named list of step outputs. Use pip_view() with tags and manual list composition for grouped output.
  • The group column has been removed from the pipeline data.table. Steps previously using group = "..." in pip_add() should use tags = "...".

Documentation

  • Comprehensive revision of all vignettes to match the new pip_* API.
  • Revised vignettes/v04-collect-output.Rmd to demonstrate tag-based grouping via pip_view() composition.
  • Updated README with a “Why use {pipeflow}” feature list, a short usage example, and a revised vs-targets summary.

Internal

  • Extensive test suite covering C++ DAG, pip_* API, aliases, execution modes, and recursive runs.
  • MIT license, updated CI workflows, dependabot config, kilo.json, lintr/styler config.
